macro_analysis.point: The Fed's hawkish hold under Warsh, with several members projecting a 2026 hike, has strengthened the USD and pushed US 10Y yields higher, which in turn pressures the Rupiah and foreign flows out of EM equities, explaining JCI's 0.55% decline as rate-sensitive sectors like Property & Real Estate (-2.29%) and Technology (-1.72%) sold off.

Bank of Japan's rate hike to 1%, the highest since 1995, has triggered Yen carry trade unwinding, weakening the Yen and pressuring Asian FX, including the Rupiah, while the Nikkei's +0.72% gain suggests domestic resilience, but for Indonesia this adds to external headwinds for foreign portfolio inflows.

Commodity weakness, with Brent crude down 0.42% and gold down 1.78%, combined with a stronger USD, has dragged Mining & Energy -1.19%, and coal proxy ITMG fell 3.53%, reflecting risk-off sentiment and lower commodity demand expectations from a hawkish Fed, which also hurts Indonesia's export revenues and the Rupiah.

Despite the hawkish Fed, BI is projected to hold rates steady at the June RDG, which may provide some Rupiah support, but the divergence between BI's hold and the Fed's hawkish stance keeps the Rupiah under pressure, as reflected in USD/IDR rising 0.19% to 17748, and foreign investor flows remain mixed across large caps like BBRI and BBCA.

The key risk to watch is whether the Fed's hawkish signals and rising US yields trigger sustained foreign outflows from JCI, particularly in rate-sensitive tech and property sectors, while the Rupiah's vulnerability to further USD strength could force BI's hand to hike rates, potentially slowing domestic growth and weighing on consumer and infrastructure names.
